label: baseline
note: Illustrative stated starting points; live provider calls, no user Chart writes.

context.intention: I maintain a consistent workout routine.
context.actualStartingPoint: I exercise sporadically. I can use three 30-minute slots each week for bodyweight exercise at home.
context.destinationDescription: I maintain a consistent workout routine.

raw.destination: Maintain a consistent workout routine with three 30-minute sessions weekly

waypoints.title: Establish a habit of exercising three times per week
waypoints.rationale: Regular exercise sessions form the foundation of a consistent routine.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Complete at least three 30-minute bodyweight exercise sessions each week for two consecutive weeks.

moves.title: Schedule three 30-minute workout slots in your weekly calendar
moves.rationale: Setting specific times increases the likelihood of following through.

moves.title: Prepare workout space and necessary materials at home
moves.rationale: Having a ready environment reduces barriers to starting.

moves.title: Start the first 30-minute bodyweight workout session this week
moves.rationale: Beginning the routine initiates the habit formation.

moves.title: Track each workout session completion in a simple log
moves.rationale: Monitoring progress supports consistency.

suggestedOneMove.title: Schedule three 30-minute workout slots in your weekly calendar
suggestedOneMove.rationale: Scheduling is the first step to committing to a consistent routine.

raw.personalizedGuidance: Start by setting fixed times for your workouts this week to build consistency gradually.

analysis.startingPointSummary: Currently exercises sporadically, with availability for three 30-minute sessions weekly at home.
assumptions: User can allocate three 30-minute slots weekly for exercise.
User has basic knowledge of bodyweight exercises or can perform simple routines at home.
analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: Completion of three 30-minute bodyweight exercise sessions per week for two consecutive weeks.
analysis.difficultyReduction: Focus on scheduling and small, manageable sessions to reduce overwhelm and build habit.

context.intention: I successfully complete my first half marathon.
context.actualStartingPoint: I run 5 km comfortably twice a week. I can train three days each week. I have never completed a half marathon.
context.destinationDescription: I successfully complete my first half marathon.

raw.destination: Complete your first half marathon successfully

waypoints.title: Increase weekly running distance to 15 km
waypoints.rationale: Building endurance by increasing total weekly running distance is essential for half marathon readiness.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Run a total of 15 km in a week spread over training days.

moves.title: Add a 3 km run to your weekly schedule
moves.rationale: Adding a small run increases weekly mileage gradually.

moves.title: Increase one existing run from 5 km to 6 km
moves.rationale: Gradually lengthening runs improves endurance safely.

moves.title: Plan running days to spread out the 15 km evenly
moves.rationale: Balanced distribution helps recovery and consistency.

waypoints.title: Run at least one 10 km run comfortably
waypoints.rationale: Being comfortable running 10 km shows readiness to handle longer distances.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Complete a 10 km run without excessive fatigue or injury.

moves.title: Schedule a 10 km run on a weekend day
moves.rationale: Setting a specific day helps commit to the longer run.

moves.title: Use pacing strategies to maintain a steady speed
moves.rationale: Consistent pacing prevents early exhaustion.

moves.title: Hydrate well before and after the run
moves.rationale: Proper hydration supports endurance and recovery.

waypoints.title: Complete a 15 km run as longest training run
waypoints.rationale: Completing a 15 km run builds confidence and physical preparation for the half marathon.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Successfully complete a 15 km run during training without injury.

moves.title: Plan a 15 km run route in a safe environment
moves.rationale: Knowing the route reduces stress and logistical issues.

moves.title: Run the 15 km at a comfortable pace
moves.rationale: Avoiding overexertion helps complete the distance safely.

moves.title: Rest the day before and after the long run
moves.rationale: Recovery is crucial to prevent injury and fatigue.

waypoints.title: Maintain consistent training of three runs per week for 8 weeks
waypoints.rationale: Consistency over time builds endurance and running habit.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Complete three runs per week for eight consecutive weeks.

moves.title: Set a weekly running schedule with fixed days
moves.rationale: Routine supports habit formation and consistency.

moves.title: Track each run completed in a training log
moves.rationale: Monitoring progress encourages accountability.

moves.title: Adjust runs as needed to avoid injury
moves.rationale: Listening to your body helps sustain training.

waypoints.title: Complete the half marathon race successfully
waypoints.rationale: Finishing the race marks achievement of the goal.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Cross the finish line of the half marathon without dropping out.

moves.title: Register for a half marathon race
moves.rationale: Official registration commits you to the goal.

moves.title: Taper training in the week before the race
moves.rationale: Reducing training load aids recovery and performance.

moves.title: Plan race day logistics including nutrition and pacing
moves.rationale: Preparation helps manage stress and energy during the race.

suggestedOneMove.title: Add a 3 km run to your weekly schedule
suggestedOneMove.rationale: Starting with a small increase in weekly distance is manageable and builds endurance.

raw.personalizedGuidance: Gradually increase your running distance and build endurance with consistent training three days a week to prepare for your half marathon.

analysis.startingPointSummary: Currently runs 5 km comfortably twice a week, training three days weekly is possible, no half marathon completed yet.
assumptions: The user can increase running distance safely without injury.
The user can commit to training three times per week consistently.
The user has access to safe running routes for longer distances.
analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: User runs 10 km comfortably, indicating increased endurance.
analysis.difficultyReduction: Breaking the goal into incremental distance increases and consistency milestones makes the plan manageable.

context.actualStartingPoint: Anchor is launched with 20 paying users. I am the solo developer, with 10 hours a week for growth and no paid advertising budget. I can contact current users and have subscription analytics.

vision.title: A sustainable Anchor business
vision.description: 10,000 paying users who continue using Anchor

waypoints.title: Reach 200 paying users
waypoints.rationale: Growing paying users steadily shows early traction and validates acquisition strategies.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Subscription analytics show at least 200 active paying users.

moves.title: Analyze subscription analytics to identify user segments with highest retention
moves.rationale: Understanding who stays helps focus growth efforts.

moves.title: Contact current paying users for feedback on product value and improvement areas
moves.rationale: User insights inform retention and acquisition tactics.

moves.title: Implement small product improvements based on user feedback
moves.rationale: Enhancements can increase user satisfaction and retention.

moves.title: Engage current users with regular updates and community outreach
moves.rationale: Active engagement supports retention and word-of-mouth growth.

waypoints.title: Establish a repeatable user acquisition process
waypoints.rationale: A reliable acquisition method is essential for scalable growth to thousands of users.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Documented and tested user acquisition process that consistently brings new paying users without paid ads.

moves.title: Research and select low-cost or free marketing channels suitable for Anchor
moves.rationale: Channels must fit budget constraints.

moves.title: Develop content or referral incentives to attract new users
moves.rationale: Attractive offers encourage sign-ups.

moves.title: Test acquisition tactics on a small scale and measure conversion rates
moves.rationale: Testing reveals effective strategies.

moves.title: Refine and document the acquisition process based on test results
moves.rationale: Documentation enables repeatability and scaling.

waypoints.title: Improve user retention to reduce churn
waypoints.rationale: Retaining users sustains growth and increases lifetime value.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Implemented retention strategies that demonstrably reduce churn rate.

moves.title: Analyze churn data to identify common drop-off points
moves.rationale: Knowing when and why users leave guides retention efforts.

moves.title: Develop and implement retention features or communication strategies
moves.rationale: Targeted actions can keep users engaged.

moves.title: Monitor retention metrics after changes to assess impact
moves.rationale: Measurement confirms effectiveness.

moves.title: Iterate on retention tactics based on user feedback and data
moves.rationale: Continuous improvement sustains retention gains.

waypoints.title: Reach 1,000 paying users
waypoints.rationale: Scaling to 1,000 users confirms growth and retention strategies are working.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Subscription analytics show at least 1,000 active paying users.

moves.title: Scale up successful acquisition tactics to reach more users
moves.rationale: Expanding proven methods grows user base.

moves.title: Enhance onboarding experience to convert more sign-ups to paying users
moves.rationale: Better onboarding increases conversion rates.

moves.title: Maintain engagement and retention efforts at larger scale
moves.rationale: Sustained retention supports growth.

moves.title: Leverage user testimonials and referrals to attract new users
moves.rationale: Social proof aids acquisition.

waypoints.title: Reach 10,000 paying users
waypoints.rationale: Achieving 10,000 paying users fulfills the vision of a sustainable Anchor business.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Subscription analytics show at least 10,000 active paying users.

moves.title: Optimize and automate acquisition and retention processes
moves.rationale: Automation supports efficient scaling.

moves.title: Expand outreach through partnerships or organic growth channels
moves.rationale: Broader reach attracts more users.

moves.title: Continuously monitor analytics to maintain growth and retention
moves.rationale: Data-driven adjustments sustain success.

moves.title: Plan for product and support scaling to handle larger user base
moves.rationale: Infrastructure readiness ensures user satisfaction.

suggestedOneMove.title: Analyze subscription analytics to identify user segments with highest retention
suggestedOneMove.rationale: Understanding who stays helps focus growth efforts.

raw.personalizedGuidance: Focus first on understanding your current users and retention to build a foundation for sustainable growth.

analysis.startingPointSummary: Anchor is launched with 20 paying users; solo developer with 10 hours/week and no paid ads; has subscription analytics and user contact access.
assumptions: User feedback and analytics are reliable for guiding improvements.
Low-cost or free marketing channels can be identified and leveraged.
Retention improvements will positively impact churn rates.
analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: Current paying users count 20; subscription analytics available to track growth to 200 users.
analysis.difficultyReduction: Breaking growth into milestones of 200, 1,000, and 10,000 paying users reduces complexity and sets achievable targets.
